Dewan Ekonomi Nasional · PHK Early-Warning Dashboard

Provincial Structure Indices — Finalists

A clean comparison of the candidate labour-structure and economic-structure indices for the Layoff Pressure Index. Each is a per-year cross-sectional PCA over 38 provinces (2022–2025), validated against recorded PHK — which is only ever a validation target, never a PCA input. Every model shows full diagnostics, its variable correlation matrix, and the provincial score distribution.

How to read every model

KMO (sampling adequacy) should be ≥0.6 — green is healthy, red <0.5 is unacceptable. Factors = eigenvalues >1 (Kaiser); 1 means a single clean dimension. Cond# = condition number; >100 (red) signals severe multicollinearity. Spear rate = rank correlation of the index with PHK per 100k formal workers (the headline validation); Spear tot uses total PHK. In the correlation matrix, deeper colour = stronger |r|. In loadings, red MSA flags a variable below the 0.5 floor (inert).

1 · Indeks Struktur Ketenagakerjaan

Five-variable formal-vs-informal structure. Two finalists — Model 7 (agriculture marker) and Model 9 (manufacturing marker) — each shown twice: with underemployment (the recommended hidden-slack measure) and with open unemployment (TPT) swapped in, to document why underemployment wins.

The best-validating labour index. A single clean factor (KMO 0.72, 1 Kaiser factor). The formal-vs-informal block dominates: formal ↔ full-time +0.90, formal ↔ agriculture −0.89. Underemployment loads negative — hidden slack marks the informal/agrarian end that formal PHK bypasses, which is exactly why it validates best (Spear-rate 0.44 in 2025).

Industrial marker instead of agrarian. Manufacturing sits far looser in the matrix (+0.36 with formal vs agriculture's −0.89), so it is the least redundant fifth variable, and the factor is clean in 2022–2024 (KMO 0.65–0.78). In 2025, once Papua Pegunungan is included (92.5% agriculture, ~0.08% manufacturing, low formal), it acts as a structural outlier that pulls KMO down to 0.65 and opens a second factor. Ranking stays ~99% aligned with Model 7; validation is a shade lower (0.40). This sensitivity to one extreme province is the main reason Model 7 (agriculture marker, no such gap) is the steadier choice.

Underemployment → TPT. The factor stays clean (KMO up to 0.76) but validation drops sharply (0.44 → 0.32). TPT (open unemployment) loads positive — it rises with formality/development rather than marking distress — so it reinforces the formal axis without adding the hidden-slack signal. It also loses Kepulauan Riau in 2022–23 (TPT unavailable).

Model 9 with TPT. Same story — validation falls to 0.30 and PC1 weakens (55%). In a dual, informal, safety-net-thin economy, distress hides as underemployment, not open unemployment; TPT is the wrong slack marker for a layoff-exposure index.

Full 13-variable set — invalid. Condition number >180,000, KMO 0.27, four Kaiser factors. Stuffing every expenditure and sector share (which sum to identities) plus per-capita/poverty/NPL into one PCA produces a near-singular matrix. High validation here is meaningless — the factor is not identified.

The clean index. Dropping the two reference categories (consumption, services) and the inert own-axis variable (mining, MSA 0.14) yields KMO 0.70, a single Kaiser factor, condition # 13, all MSA ≥ 0.66. PC1 reads as trade-integrated & industrial ↔ domestic & agrarian (export/import/manuf positive; agri/government negative) and validates best of all — Spear-rate 0.66 in 2025.

3 · Verdict

Labour structure

Model 7 (formal · agri · full-time · underemployment · average wage) is the best-validating single factor. Model 9 (manufacturing instead of agriculture) is 99% concordant and clean in 2022–2024, but sensitive to one extreme province (Papua Pegunungan) in 2025 — a defensible alternative if the industrial framing is preferred, though Model 7 is steadier. Keep underemployment, not TPT: TPT is development-linked and drops validation ~0.12 while costing coverage.

Economic structure

Use the 5-variable index: government · export · import · manuf · agri (÷ PDRB). It is the only specification that is both a valid single factor and the strongest validator (0.66). Never combine full share-sets — the condition number explodes. Poverty and sector productivity were tested and did not earn a place (they lower KMO or sit inert).

All indices are unsupervised (PCA on standardised variables); PHK enters only at validation. Correlations are moderate (0.3–0.7) by design — these map structural exposure, not a forecast. Cross-section is one row per province per year; scores are 0–100 min–max rescaled within each year.
